layout: 3 columns x 2 rows, transparent photographic cutouts
first: Carassius carassius, Perca fluviatilis, Cyprinus carpio, Tinca tinca, Rutilus rutilus, Scardinius erythrophthalmus
sheets: 1 Amur sleeper Perccottus glenii: stout brown mottled head, huge mouth, rounded tail; 2 Common bleak Alburnus alburnus: slender bright silver body, forked tail, upturned mouth; 3 White bream Blicca bjoerkna: deep flattened silvery body, small head, long anal fin; 4 Gudgeon Gobio gobio: slim mottled brown body, inferior mouth with TWO short barbels, spotted fins; 5 European weatherfish Misgurnus fossilis: long eel-like tan-brown body with horizontal dark stripes, tiny fins, several fine mouth barbels; 6 Grass carp Ctenopharyngodon idella: streamlined thick grey-silver body, large dark-edged scales, no mouth barbels.

1 Bighead carp Hypophthalmichthys nobilis: huge broad head, low-set eyes, mottled grey silver body, no barbels; 2 Wels catfish Silurus glanis: long broad flat head, huge wide mouth, TWO very long upper barbels and four short lower barbels, scaleless olive-mottled skin, exceptionally long anal fin merging toward rounded tail, tiny dorsal fin near head, NOT a carp or shark; 3 Smallmouth buffalo Ictiobus bubalus: thick high-backed grey-bronze body, small downturned sucker mouth, long dorsal fin; 4 Golden crucian Carassius carassius: natural bronze-gold round-scaled body, small mouth WITHOUT barbels, short ordinary tail; 5 Black carp Mylopharyngodon piceus: elongate thick slate-black body, dark large scales, no barbels; 6 Largemouth bass Micropterus salmoides: olive body with dark horizontal flank band, very large hinged mouth extending beyond eye, spiny dorsal joined to soft dorsal.

1 Pumpkinseed sunfish Lepomis gibbosus: deep round blue-green golden mottled body, orange-red belly, black operculum spot edged orange, blue lines on cheek; 2 Northern snakehead Channa argus: long cylindrical brown mottled body, flattened snake-like head, large mouth, long dorsal and anal fins, rounded tail; 3 Nile tilapia Oreochromis niloticus: deep grey-silver body, faint vertical bands, long spiny dorsal and vertically striped rounded tail; 4 Mirror carp Cyprinus carpio mirror morph: thick brown-gold body with sparse very LARGE irregular mirror scales along lateral line, obvious mouth barbels; 5 Silver carp Hypophthalmichthys molitrix: streamlined silvery body, broad head, small eyes placed low below mouth level, no barbels; 6 American paddlefish Polyodon spathula: long broad flat paddle-shaped rostrum nearly a third of body, smooth grey skin, heterocercal tail, distinct gill covers. Include entire paddle.

1 Common bream Abramis brama: very deep laterally compressed bronze-silver body, small protrusible mouth, very long dark anal fin; 2 Zander Sander lucioperca: long torpedo-shaped silver-olive body with faint dark vertical bars, pointed head, large canine mouth, TWO SEPARATE dorsal fins first with tall sharp spines, large forked tail, NOT round perch; 3 Northern pike Esox lucius: very long olive-green body with pale yellow oval spots, flattened duckbill snout, rear-set dorsal and anal fins near tail; 4 Lake trout Salvelinus namaycush: long grey-green body with many cream pale spots, strongly forked tail, white fin margins, adipose fin; 5 Eurasian ruffe Gymnocephalus cernua: small mottled grey-olive perch-like body, large continuous spiny dorsal fin, big eye, downward small mouth; 6 Common dace Leuciscus leuciscus: sleek silvery small-scaled body, grey fins, forked tail, slender silver minnow shape.

1 Blue bream Ballerus ballerus: deep compressed silver body with blue-grey back and very long narrow anal fin; 2 White-eye bream Ballerus sapa: silvery deep narrow body, very large bright silver iris, long anal fin, blunt short snout; 3 Burbot Lota lota: mottled brown-green eel-shaped body, one small chin barbel, two dorsal fins second extremely long, rounded tail; 4 Common whitefish Coregonus lavaretus: silver grey streamlined salmonid, small downturned mouth, adipose fin, forked dark tail; 5 Vendace Coregonus albula: slender small silver salmonid, upturned lower jaw, blackish back, adipose fin; 6 Ide Leuciscus idus: robust deep silver-gold scaled body, orange-red lower fins, blunt head, large forked tail.

1 Sabrefish Pelecus cultratus: long compressed silver body, sharply upcurved belly like a sabre, strongly upturned mouth, long anal fin; 2 Asp Leuciscus aspius: long silvery predator body, large upturned toothless mouth, pointed grey dorsal and forked tail; 3 Alpine char Salvelinus alpinus: grey-green body with pale and red spots, orange belly, white-edged pectoral pelvic and anal fins, adipose fin; 4 Brown trout Salmo trutta: olive-golden body with black and red haloed spots, short rounded snout, adipose fin; 5 Peled Coregonus peled: deep high-backed silver salmonid, small head, small mouth, adipose fin; 6 Muksun Coregonus muksun: large silver whitefish, dark back, fleshy blunt snout projecting over small subterminal mouth, adipose fin.

1 Siberian taimen Hucho taimen: elongated large salmonid, powerful broad head, olive speckled back, copper reddish body and red tail, adipose fin; 2 Siberian sturgeon Acipenser baerii: long grey body with FIVE distinct rows of bony scutes, pointed shovel snout, ventral mouth and short barbels, sharklike heterocercal tail, NOT a shark; 3 Beluga sturgeon Huso huso: huge thick pale grey body, short upturned blunt snout, very large ventral crescent mouth, bony scutes and four barbels, heterocercal tail; 4 Sterlet Acipenser ruthenus: slender grey-brown sturgeon with very LONG sharply pointed snout, fringed four mouth barbels, numerous small pale lateral bony scutes, heterocercal tail; 5 Nelma Stenodus leucichthys nelma: elongate bright silver salmonid with big pointed mouth and dark fins, adipose fin; 6 Broad whitefish Coregonus nasus: broad thick silver body, small head, bulbous blunt snout, small inferior mouth, forked tail and adipose fin.

1 European sardine Sardina pilchardus: slender silver body, blue-green back, faint dark spots behind gill; 2 Atlantic mackerel Scomber scombrus: torpedo-shaped metallic blue-green back covered with dark wavy vertical stripes, silver belly, tiny finlets near tail; 3 Atlantic bluefin tuna Thunnus thynnus: muscular thick metallic deep-blue body, silver belly, short pectoral fins, yellow finlets near crescent tail; 4 Long-snouted seahorse Hippocampus guttulatus: upright curved equine head and LONG tube snout, curled prehensile tail, knobby bony body, tan-brown mottled camouflage, full body SIDE VIEW upright; 5 European sprat Sprattus sprattus: small narrow silver herring body, blue-green back, keeled belly; 6 European anchovy Engraulis encrasicolus: small slender silver fish, very LARGE mouth extending behind eye, short snout, silver lateral stripe.

1 Atlantic horse mackerel Trachurus trachurus: silver-blue streamlined fish, very large eye and bony raised scutes along curved lateral line; 2 Black goby Gobius niger: brown mottled squat fish, broad rounded head, large pectoral fins, two dorsal fins, rounded tail; 3 Red mullet Mullus barbatus: pinkish-red silver elongated body, gently sloping forehead, TWO long chin barbels clearly visible; 4 Atlantic herring Clupea harengus: long silver compressed body, blue-green back, forked tail, single short dorsal fin; 5 European flounder Platichthys flesus: flat asymmetric oval brown mottled body, both eyes on upper side, fringed dorsal and anal fins around body, top-oblique view; 6 Flathead grey mullet Mugil cephalus: blunt broad flat head, silver-grey cylindrical body with dark horizontal stripes, two short separated dorsal fins.

1 Garfish Belone belone: extremely long thin silver-green body, very long needlelike upper and lower jaws, dorsal and anal fins near tail; 2 Redfish Sebastes norvegicus: orange-red spiny stout body, very large eye, bony spiked head, spiny dorsal fin; 3 Gilthead seabream Sparus aurata: deep silvery oval body, unmistakable GOLD band BETWEEN EYES and dark opercular spot, short small mouth, spiny dorsal; 4 European seabass Dicentrarchus labrax: long lean silver body, grey-green back, large dark gill-cover spot, TWO dorsal fins, pointed mouth; 5 Atlantic halibut Hippoglossus hippoglossus: large long diamond-shaped flatfish, both eyes on upper side, dark brown body, strong crescent tail, top-oblique view; 6 Northern red snapper Lutjanus campechanus: rich pink-red deep body, triangular head, large red iris, pointed spiny dorsal and forked red tail.

1 Dusky grouper Epinephelus marginatus: very thick robust brown mottled body, huge thick-lipped mouth, rounded tail with pale edge, golden mottled sides; 2 Great barracuda Sphyraena barracuda: very long narrow silver body, large pointed head and protruding lower jaw with sharp teeth, dark blotches, separated dorsal fins; 3 Spiny dogfish Squalus acanthias: slender small grey shark, pale flank spots, pointed snout, two dorsal fins with small spines, NO anal fin, heterocercal tail; 4 Common stingray Dasyatis pastinaca: smooth brown diamond shaped disc, long thin whip tail with barb, dorsal top view, entire tail visible; 5 Cobia Rachycentron canadum: elongated brown-grey body with dark lateral stripe and cream belly, broad flat head, small isolated dorsal spines then long dorsal fin; 6 European seabass Dicentrarchus labrax: lean silver fish, grey back, dark gill-cover spot, TWO separate dorsal fins, spiny first dorsal.

1 Common clownfish Amphiprion ocellaris: small bright orange fish with THREE broad WHITE vertical bands bordered black, rounded fins, side view; 2 Swordfish Xiphias gladius: long metallic blue-silver muscular body, very LONG FLAT straight swordbill, tall curved dorsal fin, crescent tail, full bill visible; 3 Atlantic blue marlin Makaira nigricans: blue back and silver flanks with cobalt vertical bars, long ROUND spear bill, tall anterior dorsal fin tapering into low dorsal, crescent tail, include full bill; 4 Giant oceanic manta Mobula birostris: huge triangular black-grey winglike fins, broad central body, two curled cephalic head lobes, slender whip tail, top dorsal view, entire silhouette; 5 Flying fish Exocoetus volitans: silver-blue slender body, exceptionally enlarged winglike pectoral fins spread wide, forked tail with long lower lobe; 6 Roundnose grenadier Coryphaenoides rupestris: deep-sea grey-brown fish with large head and eye, very long thin tapering rat-like tail and NO separate caudal fin.

1 Marbled rockcod Notothenia rossii: stout brown-olive mottled cold-water fish, blunt head, broad pectoral fins and continuous soft dorsal, rounded tail; 2 Black seabream Spondyliosoma cantharus: deep oval silver grey body, small pointed mouth, fine dark vertical stripes, long spiny dorsal; 3 Bluefish Pomatomus saltatrix: powerful streamlined blue-green fish, silver sides, large mouth with visible teeth, two dorsal fins, deeply forked tail; 4 Atlantic cod Gadus morhua: mottled green-brown body, THREE separate dorsal fins, pale curved lateral line, ONE prominent chin barbel; 5 Haddock Melanogrammus aeglefinus: silver-grey body, THREE dorsal fins first tall pointed, distinct black lateral line and black THUMBPRINT spot above pectoral fin, tiny chin barbel; 6 Saithe Pollachius virens: sleek dark green-grey back with silver body, THREE dorsal fins, nearly straight WHITE lateral line, projecting lower jaw.

1 Monkfish Lophius piscatorius: extremely broad flattened ugly brown head, HUGE broad mouth, many small pointed teeth, tiny tapered body and tail, two broad pectoral fins like arms, fishing-lure filament on head, side/top oblique view; 2 Mahi-mahi Coryphaena hippurus adult male: brilliant natural metallic golden-green flanks and blue back, tall blunt vertical forehead, long continuous blue dorsal fin, deeply forked tail; 3 Wahoo Acanthocybium solandri: extremely long streamlined silver fish with vivid cobalt vertical bars, long pointed snout, long low dorsal, finlets and crescent tail; 4 Atlantic sailfish Istiophorus albicans: long blue-silver billfish with enormous extended SAIL dorsal fin spanning body, long thin round spear bill, long pelvic filaments, crescent tail, full sail and bill visible; 5 Yellowfin tuna Thunnus albacares: blue-silver streamlined thick body, conspicuously LONG curved bright YELLOW second dorsal and anal fins, yellow finlets, crescent tail; 6 Black marlin Istiompax indica: dark steel-blue massive billfish, very powerful thick body, long round spear bill, rigid low pectoral fins and low tall-fronted dorsal, silver-grey belly.

1 Opah Lampris guttatus: very deep almost circular metallic silver-red body with white spots, bright RED fins and large RED eye, small mouth; 2 Mediterranean moray Muraena helena: thick eel-like dark brown body with irregular golden yellow marbling, blunt head and toothy mouth, NO pectoral fins, long fin ridge along body; 3 Ocean sunfish Mola mola: enormous round flattened silver-grey disc body, tall triangular dorsal and anal fins, truncated scalloped tail clavus, tiny puckered mouth, unmistakable sunfish shape; 4 Giant grouper Epinephelus lanceolatus: enormous very stocky dark olive-grey mottled body, massive broad head and mouth, thick rounded tail and small eyes; 5 Albacore Thunnus alalunga: streamlined navy-blue silver tuna, exceptionally LONG slender pectoral fins reaching far past dorsal fin, short second dorsal and crescent tail; 6 Bigeye tuna Thunnus obesus: thick blue-silver tuna with unusually LARGE EYES, moderately long pectoral fins, short yellow dorsal and anal fins, yellow finlets.

1 Brown trout stream form Salmo trutta fario: small robust bronze-olive trout with black and RED haloed spots along sides, rounded red-brown fins and adipose fin; 2 European grayling Thymallus thymallus: slender silver-purple salmonid with extremely TALL sail-shaped spotted dorsal fin, small mouth, adipose fin; 3 European eel Anguilla anguilla: very long cylindrical snake-shaped olive brown fish with cream belly, small blunt head, small pectoral fins, dorsal and anal fins merge with tail, NO barbels; 4 Chub Squalius cephalus: robust long silvery cyprinid with broad head, big terminal mouth, large dark-edged scales and orange pelvic/anal fins; 5 Common minnow Phoxinus phoxinus: tiny slender olive-silver fish, irregular dark vertical flank blotches, thin gold lateral line, small translucent rounded fins; 6 Spirlin Alburnoides bipunctatus: tiny slender silvery fish with a conspicuous double line of dark dots along curved lateral line, reddish base of fins.

1 Stone loach Barbatula barbatula: slim bottom-dwelling mottled brown fish, narrow cylindrical body, small inferior mouth with SIX barbels, rounded short fins; 2 European bullhead Cottus gobio: broad very large flattened bony head, tiny tapering brown mottled body, huge fan pectoral fins, two dorsal fins, rounded tail; 3 Spined loach Cobitis taenia: very thin elongated yellowish fish, neat row of dark rounded spots along flanks, tiny head with short barbels and suborbital spine, rounded tail; 4 Lenok Brachymystax lenok: robust bronze-brown salmonid with numerous small black spots and reddish flanks, small terminal mouth, adipose fin; 5 European river lamprey Lampetra fluviatilis: long slender olive-silver scaleless eel-like body, round SUCTION DISC mouth, SEVEN small circular gill openings behind each eye, NO paired fins, two low dorsal fins; 6 Sea trout Salmo trutta trutta: bright silver trout with black X-shaped and round spots, streamlined body, adipose fin, NOT rainbow trout.

1 Siberian taimen Hucho taimen: long powerful salmonid, olive spotted back, copper-brown flanks and vivid red-brown tail, large pointed mouth, adipose fin; 2 Rainbow trout Oncorhynchus mykiss: silver-green body, vivid natural PINK lateral stripe, many fine black spots including on tail, adipose fin; 3 Arctic char Salvelinus alpinus: dark blue-green back, pale pink-white round spots, deep orange belly, white leading edges on lower fins, adipose fin; 4 Cherry salmon Oncorhynchus masou in ocean phase: bright silver body with small black spots above lateral line, short powerful head, forked grey tail and adipose fin; 5 Chum salmon Oncorhynchus keta in spawning colors: elongated muscular olive-brown body with thick PURPLE and dark green vertical flank bars, gently hooked snout, adipose fin; 6 Pink salmon Oncorhynchus gorbuscha mature male: characteristic very large HUMPED BACK, hooked snout, olive-grey flanks with large dark oval spots on upper body and BOTH tail lobes.

1 Coho salmon Oncorhynchus kisutch ocean phase: metallic silver flanks, deep blue-green back, small black spots only on upper body and UPPER tail lobe, bright pale gums at base of teeth, adipose fin; 2 Chinook salmon Oncorhynchus tshawytscha ocean phase: large muscular steel-blue and silver body, small dark spots on back and BOTH tail lobes, black gums, big head, adipose fin; 3 Atlantic salmon Salmo salar ocean phase: slim powerful silver body with sparse dark X-shaped spots above lateral line, slightly forked tail usually without dense spots, adipose fin; 4 Sockeye salmon Oncorhynchus nerka spawning male: unmistakable vivid RED body with olive GREEN head, hooked jaw, NO black body spots, adipose fin; 5 Dolly Varden Salvelinus malma: dark green-grey body with small pink pale spots, orange lower fins with white leading edges, lightly forked tail, adipose fin; 6 Huchen Hucho hucho: long robust silvery-brown salmonid with small dark X-shaped spots on sides, large flattened pointed head, powerful mouth, grey-red fins and adipose fin.
